Modal verbs themselves do not have specific past tense forms. By using these combinations, modal verbs can convey past meanings. In negative sentences, a modal verb is typically followed by the word "not." For example, "cannot," "should not," "will not," and "must not" are negative forms of the modal verbs "can," "should," "will," and "must" respectively. Yes, modal verbs can be used in questions. When forming questions with modal verbs, the subject and the modal verb are inverted. Modal verbs are widely used in both affirmative and negative questions. **Video Description:** Modal Verbs for CAT 2026 is part of Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension (VARC) preparation.
